描述_ZN: Scenic Views of Yingtai" scroll, Qianlong, Qing dynasty, painted by Hong Li, on paper with ink brush, 29.2 cm in length and 57.5 cm in width.　　Yingtai is the collective name for the architectural complex on Nanhai Island, built in the Ming Dynasty, and most of the existing buildings were renovated and expanded during the Shunzhi and Kangxi periods of the Qing Dynasty. It faces the water on three sides and is covered with strange rocks and flowering trees. The main hall of Yingtai, Hanyuan Hall, was the place where the emperor dined with his ministers.
